Test Case: Time transfers as the wallet grows
Expected Result: Stays usable

Test Case: Mint FTs repeatedly until one denomination is exhausted
Expected Result: Counter reaches zero and stops, never goes negative
Also Check In Same Run: Exercises the floor on the burn path; the mint after exhaustion must fail cleanly rather than corrupt the counter

Test Case: Mint until one denomination counter walks down to exactly zero
Expected Result: Counter equals the real free tokens after every mint and ends at zero
Also Check In Same Run: Every mint must SUCCEED. FT-P-06 walks into a rejected mint instead, and on this fleet that rejection leaks locks before the decrement is ever reached - so the walk down has never actually been tested

Test Case: Mint an FT and transfer RBT at the same moment from one wallet
Expected Result: Both succeed and the denomination counter stays consistent
Also Check In Same Run: Both operations decrement the counter for the same DID by different code paths; the cheaper sibling of the deploy-versus-mint race

Test Case: Alternate an FT mint and a contract deploy ten times on one wallet
Expected Result: All twenty operations succeed and the counter is still correct
Also Check In Same Run: The sequential version of the same race - if this fails too, the two paths disagree even without concurrency, which is an ordering bug

Test Case: Force a denomination counter to zero with tokens still free then burn one
Expected Result: The count stays at zero and never goes negative
Also Check In Same Run: The only way to reach the clamp AT zero - no natural sequence subtracts from a counter that is already 0. FT-P-06 and FT-P-09 test the walk DOWN to zero, which is a different line
Code Ref: core/wallet/token_chain.go:1052; core/wallet/token_chain.go UpdateTokenInfo - GREATEST(count - 1, 0) floors the counter, masking a double decrement

Test Case: Mint one hundred FT batches checking the counter at every checkpoint
Expected Result: Counter consistent throughout and burnt total matches RBT consumed
Also Check In Same Run: The changed statement runs once per burnt RBT, so volume is what exercises it

Test Case: Sustained concurrent minting from several wallets at once
Expected Result: Every wallet still reconciles afterwards
Also Check In Same Run: Different DIDs, so a failure here means the burn path interferes ACROSS wallets - much broader than same-row contention

Test Case: Subscribe to a contract before it is deployed
Expected Result: Record the behaviour
Also Check In Same Run: Subscribing to a token that does not exist yet may fail or succeed - both are findings

Test Case: Subscribe immediately after deployment
Expected Result: Subscriber holds the full chain
Also Check In Same Run: The baseline case - a subscriber with nothing to catch up on

Test Case: Subscribe after the contract has already been executed once
Expected Result: Subscriber holds the full chain including the execution it missed
Also Check In Same Run: Late subscribers depend on a back-fill sync that is skipped when the contract folder already exists locally

Test Case: Subscribe after several executions have already happened
Expected Result: Subscriber holds the full chain including every execution it missed
Also Check In Same Run: The deeper the chain when a node subscribes, the more a partial back-fill would hide

Test Case: Compare contract data across nodes that subscribed at different times
Expected Result: Every subscribed node holds identical chain and token data
Also Check In Same Run: Any node with a shorter chain subscribed late and never caught up - it will still accept executes

Test Case: Deploy across a fixed ladder of thirteen values from 0.001 to 10.375
Expected Result: Every value costs exactly itself
Also Check In Same Run: Points sit either side of each boundary - 0.009/0.010, 0.999/1.000/1.001 - so the pattern of failures identifies which boundary is mishandled

Test Case: Deploy twenty contracts one after another from one wallet
Expected Result: All twenty succeed and the total equals the sum of the values
Also Check In Same Run: Small errors compound; an early failure is a deploy bug, a late one is accumulated state

Test Case: Deploy from three senders at once through one quorum
Expected Result: All succeed and the quorum counter stays consistent
Also Check In Same Run: The shared quorum is the one piece of state every lane touches at once

Test Case: Measure the NEW quorum counter drift caused by one concurrent burst
Expected Result: No denomination gap widens across the burst
Also Check In Same Run: Pledge path. Reports the DELTA, not the absolute gap - the fleet carries a permanent historical 0.023 that makes every absolute drift case red forever and would hide a real new leak

Test Case: Several contracts with subscribers joining at many different depths
Expected Result: Every subscriber matches the owner on every contract
Also Check In Same Run: Several contracts syncing at once, and joins from depth 0 to depth 10; a partial back-fill has nowhere to hide

Test Case: Compare full token detail across subscribers not just chain length
Expected Result: Value, status and position identical on every node
Also Check In Same Run: Two nodes can hold the same NUMBER of chain entries and disagree about what they say

Test Case: Subscribe while an execute is in flight
Expected Result: Subscriber ends with the same chain as the owner
Also Check In Same Run: Shorter means the in-flight entry was missed by both paths; longer means it arrived twice

Test Case: Subscribe to a contract that already has twenty entries
Expected Result: Subscriber receives the whole chain
Also Check In Same Run: The SIZE of any gap says whether back-fill fetched nothing, a window, or everything but the tail

Test Case: A later subscriber must see an earlier subscriber execute
Expected Result: All three nodes agree
Also Check In Same Run: Confirms the chain is shared state rather than owner-authored history others merely observe

Test Case: Deploy several contracts with values at the same time from one wallet
Expected Result: All succeed and each costs exactly its own value
Also Check In Same Run: The collateral split runs before the main transaction opens specifically to avoid a deadlock; concurrent deploys from one wallet are what would trigger it

Test Case: Many nodes deploying valued contracts at the same moment
Expected Result: All succeed and no quorum counter drifts
Also Check In Same Run: A pledge shortage here is a capacity result not a defect; a drifting quorum counter is a defect

Test Case: Deploy two hundred contracts checking the counter at every checkpoint
Expected Result: Counter consistent throughout and total spend matches the values
Also Check In Same Run: Reports the deploy number at which the counter FIRST drifted - early means an immediate defect, late means accumulation

Test Case: Execute one contract two hundred times
Expected Result: Chain length tracks the operation count throughout
Also Check In Same Run: Ahead of the count means duplicate entries, behind means dropped ones

Test Case: Subscribers joining continuously throughout a long execute run
Expected Result: Every subscriber matches the owner whatever depth it joined at
Also Check In Same Run: Failures grouped by join depth - a clean cutoff means a back-fill limit, scattered means a delivery race

Test Case: Every host deploying repeatedly and concurrently
Expected Result: Every wallet and every quorum still reconciles afterwards
Also Check In Same Run: Rejection rate is a capacity result; a drifting counter is a defect

Test Case: Deploy and execute alternately for a sustained period
Expected Result: Counter consistent for the whole period
Also Check In Same Run: Reports elapsed time as well as operation count - a time-dependent failure points at background work such as unpledging

Test Case: Deploy three contracts each with a value in ONE request
Expected Result: All three deploy and the total equals the sum of the values
Also Check In Same Run: The pre-pass loops over every contract in the request, so the second iteration must see what the first committed - a different path from concurrent separate requests

Test Case: Send three contracts in one request twice, with binary-exact then binary-inexact values
Expected Result: Both accepted, or both refused for the same stated reason
Also Check In Same Run: Decides between float accumulation and multi-contract being unsupported. 0.25+0.5+0.125 is exact in binary; 0.345+0.359+0.317 is not. Exact accepted and inexact refused can only be accumulation

Test Case: Send 1 contract, then 2 inexact, then 2 binary-exact, and find where it breaks
Expected Result: All three accepted
Also Check In Same Run: The ladder behind SC-C-32. N=1 rules out the guard testing individual values; holding N at 2 across exact and inexact rules out the count. 0.1+0.2 is the canonical float64 case and worth more in a PR comment than any arbitrary triple

Test Case: Deploy a small contract that SUCCEEDS and watch the committed RBT
Expected Result: Committed rises by exactly the contract value
Also Check In Same Run: The control for SC-C-27. Without it the finding reads as 'collateral was committed' which sounds correct; with it the finding is 'a rejected deploy commits the same value and gets no contract'. Also records whether a success releases it, which sets the severity

Test Case: Force a deploy to fail after its collateral split has already committed
Expected Result: Rejected, with nothing left locked and the balance restored
Also Check In Same Run: The split commits its own genesis on a separate connection before the outer transaction opens, so an outer failure does not roll it back; SC-C-06 is rejected before the lock and never reaches this

Test Case: Wait two minutes after a rejected deploy and re-read the committed RBT
Expected Result: Committed falls - the collateral is released, not lost
Also Check In Same Run: Runs immediately after SC-C-27 on the same host. Committed is TERMINAL, so if it has not moved the pre-pass loses the value on every rejected deploy. This is what makes SC-C-27 a blocker rather than a report
Code Ref: core/transaction_builder.go:170; core/transaction_builder.go SC collateral pre-pass persists the split before consensus; nothing unwinds it on rejection

Test Case: Delete a denomination counter row then burn a token of that denomination
Expected Result: The row is recreated and matches reality, or the mint is rejected
Also Check In Same Run: DELIBERATE CORRUPTION - records and restores the row. The bare UPDATE has no row to hit, so the counter would be permanently wrong with no error raised
Code Ref: core/wallet/token_chain.go; core/wallet/token_chain.go UpdateTokenInfo - UPDATE (not upsert) silently no-ops when no token_denom row exists

Test Case: Deploy a contract and mint an FT at the same moment on one DID
Expected Result: Both succeed and the denomination counter stays consistent
Also Check In Same Run: The two counter fixes write token_denom from different code paths for the same DID and do not appear to coordinate; this is the only case that runs both at once

Test Case: Compare the denomination counter against the real free tokens
Expected Result: Counter agrees at every denomination
Also Check In Same Run: Reads token_denom against the tokens table; drift here breaks a later, unrelated transaction

Test Case: Look for a phantom zero-denomination row
Expected Result: No denom=0 row exists for the DID
Also Check In Same Run: A zero row makes selection ask for tokens that cannot exist

Test Case: Check the denomination counter can never go negative
Expected Result: No denomination has a negative count
Also Check In Same Run: The burn path floors at zero deliberately; a negative count would make selection ask for an impossible number of tokens

Test Case: Check every free token has a chain row
Expected Result: No free token exists without chain history
Also Check In Same Run: Such a token counts toward the balance and the counter, so selection picks it and then validation fails

Test Case: Check no token id appears twice on one node
Expected Result: No duplicates on any host
Also Check In Same Run: The same token persisted twice - which a split retry without an ON CONFLICT guard would produce

Test Case: Check no tokens are left locked anywhere on the fleet
Expected Result: No locked tokens on any host
Also Check In Same Run: Locked is transient; anything still locked belongs to an operation that failed without releasing, and that value is stranded permanently

Test Case: Repeat one operation and record the drift after each round
Expected Result: No drift after any round
Also Check In Same Run: Distinguishes per-operation drift (grows steadily) from conditional drift (appears at one round) - the two need different fixes

Test Case: Measure how fast locks accumulate over repeated failures
Expected Result: The locked count never rises
Also Check In Same Run: Constant per failure means one release path is always missed; uneven means it depends on the failure mode

Test Case: Check committed RBT corresponds to contracts that exist
Expected Result: No host holds committed RBT without contracts
Also Check In Same Run: Committed is terminal, so collateral committed for a deploy that was rejected is lost permanently - the fleet-wide net for what SC-C-27 forces

Test Case: Check a quorum counter decrements for every token it pledges
Expected Result: Quorum counter matches its real free tokens afterwards
Also Check In Same Run: Pledge path. The counter over-states what the quorum can pledge, so it eventually fails for unrelated senders
